indicators.name: HY Credit Spreads
indicators.formula: Percentile rank of today’s spread within its own trailing 750 observations. 100 = widest in that window.

inputs.label: ICE BofA US High Yield option-adjusted spread

steps: pool = last 750 observations of BAMLH0A0HYM2, ranging 2.59 to 4.61
29 of those 750 sit below the current 2.66

indicators.name: Investment-Grade Spreads
indicators.formula: Percentile rank within its own trailing 750 observations.

inputs.label: ICE BofA US Corporate option-adjusted spread

steps: pool = last 750 observations of BAMLC0A0CM, ranging 0.73 to 1.33
234 of those 750 sit below the current 0.81

indicators.name: SOFR–IORB Spread
indicators.redundant: folded into Repo-Market Stress (45% of that composite) — weight moved there to avoid double-counting
indicators.formula: clamp(50 + (SOFR − IORB in bps) × 4, 0, 100)

indicators.name: Repo-Market Stress
indicators.formula: 0.45 × clamp(20 + (SOFR−IORB)×3) + 0.30 × clamp(20 + (SOFR−EFFR)×4) + 0.25 × clamp((SOFR 75th − 25th pctile)×4), each clamped 0–100

indicators.name: Treasury Vol Proxy (MOVE-style)
indicators.source_note: synthetic proxy from 2Y/10Y 5-day moves — the real MOVE index isn’t freely available via FRED
indicators.formula: clamp((|2Y 5-day move in bps| × 0.6 + |10Y 5-day move in bps| × 0.4) × 2, 0, 100)

indicators.name: VIX
indicators.formula: clamp((VIX − 12) × 3.2, 0, 100). Reads 0 at or below 12, saturates at about 43.

indicators.name: VIX Momentum Proxy (5D)
indicators.source_note: transform of VIX’s own 5-day change — not real futures term-structure data
indicators.formula: clamp(50 + (VIX 5-day % change) × 4, 0, 100). Reads 50 when VIX is unchanged.

indicators.name: 2Y Treasury Yield
indicators.formula: Percentile rank within its own trailing 1000 observations.
steps: pool = last 1000 observations of DGS2, ranging 3.38 to 5.19
678 of those 1000 sit below the current 4.39

indicators.name: 10Y Treasury Yield
indicators.formula: Percentile rank within its own trailing 1000 observations.
steps: pool = last 1000 observations of DGS10, ranging 3.2 to 4.98
985 of those 1000 sit below the current 4.79

indicators.name: 2s10s Curve
indicators.redundant: derived from 2Y and 10Y, both already counted separately — weight moved to Credit
indicators.formula: clamp(50 − 20 × (10Y − 2Y), 0, 100). Reads 50 at a flat curve, rises as it inverts.

indicators.name: DXY / Broad Dollar
indicators.formula: clamp((index − 100) × 2, 0, 100). Reads 0 at or below 100.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.formula: Percentile rank of the 20-observation change within its own trailing 120, inverted — so fast expansion scores low (calm).

inputs.label: Total assets, all Federal Reserve banks

steps: pool = the last 120 such changes, ranging -418,256 to 171,638

indicators.name: Bank Reserves
indicators.flag: unit-corrected (÷1000 to billions) vs. original workbook — see notes
indicators.formula: Percentile rank of the 20-observation change within its own trailing 60, inverted — so fast reserve build-up scores low (calm).

inputs.label: Reserve balances held at Federal Reserve banks

steps: pool = the last 60 such changes, ranging -559,087 to 233,002

indicators.name: Treasury General Account
indicators.flag: unit-corrected (÷1000 to billions) vs. original workbook — see notes
indicators.formula: clamp(20 + (TGA in $bn − 500) ÷ 10, 0, 100). The ÷1000 converts FRED’s $mm to the $bn the threshold assumes.

indicators.name: Financial Conditions (NFCI)
indicators.formula: Percentile rank of the 20-observation change within its own trailing 500 — fast tightening scores high.

inputs.label: Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index

steps: pool = the last 500 such changes, ranging -0.822 to 0.893

indicators.name: S&P 500 Breadth
indicators.source_note: now live via Stooq SPY/RSP — unavailable in the original workbook
indicators.formula: clamp(50 − (5-day RSP-vs-SPY spread × 10 + 20-day spread × 5), 0, 100). RSP is the equal-weight S&P, so RSP lagging SPY means a narrow market.
steps: RSP vs SPY over 5 sessions = -1.462%  (equal-weight minus cap-weight)

indicators.name: Market Participation Momentum
indicators.source_note: now live via Stooq SPY/RSP — unavailable in the original workbook
indicators.formula: clamp(50 − (5-day spread × 15 + 20-day spread × 10), 0, 100). Same inputs as Breadth, weighted harder toward the recent move.

indicators.name: Economic Surprise
indicators.formula: clamp(50 + (initial claims 5-week % change) × 5, 0, 100). Reads 50 when claims are flat.

indicators.name: Inflation & Labor Momentum
indicators.formula: clamp(50 + ((core CPI m/m × 0.5 + core PCE m/m × 0.5) − 0.2) × 200, 0, 100). Reads 50 at 0.2% monthly, roughly the 2% annual target.
steps: core CPI 336.789 vs 336.065 last month = 0.215% m/m
core PCE 130.658 vs 130.338 last month = 0.246% m/m

indicators.name: Fed Expectations
indicators.redundant: derived entirely from the 2Y Yield and SOFR-IORB scores, both already counted separately — weight moved to Credit
indicators.formula: 0.6 × (2Y yield score) + 0.4 × (SOFR–IORB score)

indicators.name: Liquidity Flow Stress
indicators.formula: Net injection = ΔFed assets + Δreserves − ΔTGA, over 5 and 20 observations. Each maps to clamp(50 − net ÷ scale), blended 65% short / 35% long. A drain scores high.

asset_outlook.note: Regime-conditioned historical tendencies from the source workbook, not guaranteed forecasts. "Relative UP" means the asset may still decline but has often held up better than broad equities.

usd_flow.note: Co-movement, not flows. Nobody publishes daily dollar flow data; this measures how the dollar moved and what moved with it. Causation runs both ways — risk-off pushes the dollar up as much as a rising dollar pushes risk assets down. Assets low on this list are not immune to the dollar, just not tracking it right now.

price_history_note: Daily closing prices and a daily-resolution reconstruction of the risk scores, both refreshed on this 15-minute schedule. Each asset is charted against a risk sub-metric grouping — but a rigorous out-of-sample test (train/test split, no regime bucket, one metric tested per asset independently) found a real, holding-up relationship for only 1 of 22 assets: Short Treasuries / T-Bills vs. Fed Balance Sheet (marked with a ✓ badge below). Every other pairing here is an illustrative grouping, not a validated predictor. "Real-time" here means "as of the latest 15-minute refresh, using the latest available daily close" — not intraday tick data.
